_comment: STEP A0's REGISTER — read by tools/check-scope-sites.py. Every `scopeOf(env)` call site in
worker.js must be either CONVERTED (gone) or DECLARED here with a reason. An unclassified site
is red. scopeOf() is the ONLY function that reads ESTATE_ID, so this list IS the inventory of
places that still take the household from config — converting them is the multi-tenancy flip.
KEYED BY ENCLOSING FUNCTION, NEVER BY LINE — deliberately. Three file:line citations went stale
inside single afternoons on 2026-09-12, every one from a concurrent insertion rather than a
change to the thing cited. `count` is load-bearing: it stops a declaration written today from
silently covering a site added tomorrow.
A REASON IS NOT AN AUDIT. The tool records that a human gave one; it cannot judge whether it is
good. And it reads SOURCE, NOT BEHAVIOUR — whether a converted site resolves the RIGHT grant is
step A15's falsifier at dev, and neither covers the other.
⛔ EMPTY ON PURPOSE AT A0. The plan runs the classifier BEFORE any conversion, so a full-red
first run is the intended reading: 58 sites, none yet examined. A2 converts B-CALLER, A3
converts B-CACHE, A4 DECLARES B-DEPLOY here rather than converting it.

baseline.note: the A0 inventory; `converted` is measured against this number

doorRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · A rate limit is an ABUSE control on the ORIGIN, not a household fact. Scoped per estate it would multiply: one attacker gets N x the budget by naming N households, and under one origin naming a household is free. Correct as the deployment's forever.

feedbackRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. ⚠️ It also guards the CREDENTIAL-FREE capture POST, which has no household to scope to even in principle.

probeRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. Guards /api/account/available, which is pre-account by construction — there is no estate at the moment it runs.

recoverRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. Guards the recovery route, whose whole premise is a person who cannot reach their household; scoping its limiter to that household would be circular.

storeDoorRecord.reason: door · ⛔ A DOOR RECORD PRECEDES ANY HOUSEHOLD BY CONSTRUCTION. watch-door.py's own rule is that it reports what happened AT a door, never who was standing at it; records carry personId:null and a deviceId is a browser bucket. The reading it exists for is the SILENT case — someone arrived and neither got in nor reported a failure — and that person has no estate to file under by definition.

handleDoor.reason: door · the read side of storeDoorRecord; same scope or the channel cannot be read back.

grantFor.reason: grant (LEGACY FALLBACK) · ⛔⛔ THIS ONE IS NOT PERMANENT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SETTLED. It looks a grant up at keyFor(scopeOf(env),'grant',hash) and then rejects row.estateId !== env.ESTATE_ID, so a foreign grant fails TWICE — wrong namespace, and rejected if it were not. Both halves must change for one deployment to serve many estates, and the LOOKUP is the harder half: a token must resolve WITHOUT already knowing which estate to look in. It is declared here as the CURRENT state with its reason, not as a decision that it stays. It is step A6's object (the grant:<personId>:<estateId> edge), and it is why A3's check cannot pass before the conversion.  ⭐ SITE 2, ADDED WITH A6 (2026-09-12): storeResolveRecord(env, scopeOf(env), …) — the instrumentation for resolveByEdge()'s two non-lookup branches. It is the DEPLOYMENT's record on purpose and not the household's: the thing being counted is that this deployment could not tell WHICH of a person's houses a request meant, which is a fact about the deployment's resolver and not about either house. Filing it under one of the candidate estates would attribute an ambiguity to whichever house happened to win. ⚠️ It carries an outcome and a COUNT of candidates — never a personId, never an estateId — so nothing household-shaped is in the row to misfile. ⛔ A7 deletes the branch this records; the site goes with it.

handleAmbient.reason: cache (B-DEPLOY, DECLARED NOT CONVERTED) · stays on scopeOf because AMBIENT_MAC is a per-deployment Worker secret - the key correctly reflects deployment-wide data. ⛔ This is BY CONSTRUCTION, not by design forever: the day a household can declare its own station credential this site must be reconverted. [paul-ruled 2026-09-13, with that risk stated to him].  ⭐ THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THE RULING, so nobody re-derives it: handleAmbient reads the station MAC at `const mac = (env.AMBIENT_MAC || "").trim()` — a per-deployment Worker SECRET since 2026-09-04 (`wrangler.toml:45`), never caller-supplied. ⚠️ worker.js's own comment above the handler still says `[vars] AMBIENT_MAC` from C5 7c (2026-09-03) — that is one day stale and the binding moved to a secret; the RULING rests on per-deployment, which both eras satisfy. The cache key's household-identifying suffix is therefore the DEPLOYMENT's own station, so the key is already exactly as specific as the data behind it. Gating the route would not change that, and converting it would make the key ASSERT a per-household scoping the data does not have — a key that claims more than it knows. ⚠️ It is the one site in this register whose reason is about the DATA rather than about the caller: the other three B-CACHE sites (airnow · drought · today-line) converted at A3 because their suffix is the CALLER's coordinates, county and canon. ⛔ The separate question — SHOULD /api/ambient be gated at all (it is deliberately ungated since 2026-08-02 so Mom's unpaired devices keep working) — is untouched by this ruling and stays open.

handleChat.reason: chat-budget · a daily model-spend CEILING is a deployment-wide control. Per-estate budget keys would give every household its own ceiling, so the origin's total spend would become unbounded in the number of households — the opposite of what a ceiling is for.

_declared_note: ⛔ DECLARED means: this site STAYS on scopeOf(env) BY DESIGN. It does NOT mean 'not yet converted'.
A site awaiting a later slice must stay UNCLASSIFIED — declaring it would launder PENDING into
BY DESIGN, the instrument would read green, and the pass that owed the work would skip it because
the tool said it was handled. That is 'an unchecked box is not open work' inverted into its more
dangerous direction: marking open work CLOSED.
⚠️ `grantFor` is the one row here that is NOT permanent, and it says so in its own reason.
_unclassified_note: ⛔ WHY 20 SITES ARE STILL UNCLASSIFIED (24 before A3), AND WHY THAT IS THE CORRECT READING RATHER THAN UNFINISHED WORK.
✅ B-CACHE IS DONE (A3, 2026-09-13) — this paragraph used to say all four were pending. handleAirNow
· handleDrought · handleTodayLine are CONVERTED: each dispatches BELOW the capability gate and is named
in MEMBER_OK, so every caller carries a resolved grant and the key is now the CALLER's estate.
⭐ handleTodayLine is the one worth knowing about — it ALREADY HELD the resolved scope (canonFor(env,
scope) reads the caller's canon two lines up) and still keyed by the deployment, so the line was
written ABOUT one household and filed UNDER another. A parameter arriving is not a parameter used.
handleAmbient is DECLARED above rather than converted, [paul-ruled 2026-09-13] — read the reason there,
and note it is NOT permanent.
THE PRE-AUTH CAPTURE PAIR — handleFeedback (2) · handleZoneAudio (4) · handleEstateFound (1). These
run BEFORE a grant exists by construction, so there is nothing to thread. They are NOT 'deployment-
scoped by design' — they are UNATTRIBUTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, which is a different reason and would be
lost if collapsed into a B-DEPLOY declaration. Measured 2026-09-12: credential-free capture is a
LEGACY-ONLY affordance (legacy 11/11 credential-free; home 0/17), and legacy keeps its own deployment,
so nothing is stranded today. It becomes live when Mom moves.
⚠️ fetch(dispatcher) — 13 SITES OF MIXED CLASS IN ONE 'FUNCTION', AND THE REGISTER CANNOT EXPRESS
THAT. Keyed by enclosing function with a count, a single declaration would cover all thirteen with one
reason, and they do not share one. Most are the ACCOUNT/SESSION/GRANT layer that steps A6 (the grant
edge), A9 (the estates array), A11 (the sign-in page) and A13 (/api/account/available) REWRITE — so
they are PENDING, and declaring them would launder pending into by-design exactly as the note above
forbids. Three of the thirteen do look genuinely deployment-wide (chat-budget :4241, the obmetrics
ratelimit :4486, accountFor :4547); they are deliberately NOT declared yet, because classifying a site
inside a block the door steps are about to rewrite is a guess about code that does not exist.
⭐ A4 RE-RUNS AFTER THE DOOR STEPS LAND. That is the honest sequence, and the count dropping from 13
is how anyone will know it happened.
